weekly: Introduction to the scope, objectives, and organization of the course. Brief review of plant classification and identification principles covered in LAUD 241, followed by an introduction to the general characteristics and classification of gymnosperms.

Gymnosperms: Ginkgoaceae, Taxaceae, Cycadaceae, Araucariaceae Study of Ginkgoaceae, Taxaceae, Cycadaceae, Araucariaceae families focusing on morphological characteristics, ecological requirements, and landscape design potential. The theoretical session is followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus.

Study of Pinaceae family focusing on morphological characteristics, ecological requirements, and landscape design potential. The theoretical session is followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus.
Gymnosperms: Pinaceae (continued) Continuation of Pinaceae family studies, followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus.
Gymnosperms: Pinaceae (continued) Continuation of Pinaceae family studies, followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus.

Gymnosperms: Cupressaceae Study of Cupressaceae family focusing on morphological characteristics, ecological requirements, and landscape design potential. The theoretical session is followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus.
Gymnosperms: Cupressaceae (continued) Continuation of Cupressaceae family studies, followed by field identification exercises with selected plant species on campus
Off-Campus Field Identification Exercise

Gymnosperms: Laboratory Exam and Mid-Term Exam Plant identification examination covering the gymnosperm species studied during the first half of the course, followed by a mid-term examination assessing the related theoretical content.

Introduction to Herbaceous Landscape Plants & Final Project Brief Introduction to the major groups of herbaceous plants used in landscape design, with emphasis on growth habits, life cycles, ecological requirements, seasonal characteristics, and design functions. Introduction of the final planting design project.

Turfgrasses and Groundcovers Study of major turfgrass and groundcover groups focusing on ecological requirements, establishment and maintenance principles, functional characteristics, and landscape applications. The theoretical session is followed by project development and desk critiques.

Annuals, Biennials and Herbaceous Perennials Study of annual, biennial, and perennial herbaceous plants focusing on life cycles, seasonal performance, morphological and visual characteristics, ecological requirements, and their roles in planting compositions. The theoretical session is followed by project development and desk critiques.

Geophytes: Bulbous, Cormous, Rhizomatous and Tuberous Plants Study of geophytes according to their underground storage structures, seasonal growth cycles, ecological requirements, and landscape design potential. The theoretical session is followed by project development and desk critiques.
Planting Design Project: Final Development & Review Final development of the planting design project through desk critiques and a comprehensive review of the course content.

weekly: Introduction: Climate crisis, ecological design, and course framework; introduction to climate justice
Landscape Ecology: Structure, function, and dynamics of socio-ecological systems
Climate as Socio-Ecological Crisis: Environmental limits, human impacts, inequality, and vulnerability
Climate Justice: Equity, environmental justice, and uneven geographies of climate risk
Climate Risks: Heat stress, flooding, water scarcity, biodiversity loss
Fieldwork: Site introduction; data collection; ecological and climatic mapping
Analytical Frameworks: Landscape analysis, risk mapping, vulnerability assessment
Presentation of research and site analysis
Environmental Limits: Carrying capacity, thresholds, resilience, adaptive capacity
Design Solutions: Nature-Based and regenerative design strategies, ecosystem-based adaptation
Governance and Implementation: Policy frameworks, planning instruments, and multi-actor collaboration in climate-responsive design
Synthesis: From Analysis to Design: Development of design concepts and strategies
Project Development and Critiques: Refinement of ecological and climate justice design proposals
Final Review: Integrated Ecological Design Proposals
